deck.title: Physical Properties of the Group 17 Elements

back_blocks.md: **Volatility** is the ease with which a substance evaporates. A volatile substance has a **low boiling point**. In Group 17, fluorine is the most volatile and iodine the least volatile.

cards.back_md: **Volatility** is the ease with which a substance evaporates. A volatile substance has a **low boiling point**. In Group 17, fluorine is the most volatile and iodine the least volatile.

front_blocks.md: Why do boiling points of the halogens increase going down Group 17?

back_blocks.md: Going down Group 17, the halogen molecules have more **electrons**. This leads to stronger **instantaneous dipole-induced dipole** (van der Waals') forces between molecules. More energy is needed to separate the molecules, raising the **boiling point**.

cards.front_md: Why do boiling points of the halogens increase going down Group 17?
cards.back_md: Going down Group 17, the halogen molecules have more **electrons**. This leads to stronger **instantaneous dipole-induced dipole** (van der Waals') forces between molecules. More energy is needed to separate the molecules, raising the **boiling point**.

front_blocks.md: Bond strength in Group 17 increases going down the group.

back_blocks.md: Bond strength generally **decreases** going down Group 17. As atoms get larger, the bonding pair of electrons is further from the nuclei and less strongly attracted to them, weakening the covalent bond.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Bond strength in Group 17 increases going down the group.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Bond strength generally **decreases** going down Group 17. As atoms get larger, the bonding pair of electrons is further from the nuclei and less strongly attracted to them, weakening the covalent bond.

front_blocks.md: Fluorine has a **..........**  bond enthalpy than chlorine because lone pair **..........**  between fluorine atoms weakens the F–F bond.

back_blocks.md: Fluorine has a **lower** bond enthalpy than chlorine because lone pair **repulsion** between fluorine atoms weakens the F–F bond.

cards.front_md: Fluorine has a **..........**  bond enthalpy than chlorine because lone pair **..........**  between fluorine atoms weakens the F–F bond.
cards.back_md: Fluorine has a **lower** bond enthalpy than chlorine because lone pair **repulsion** between fluorine atoms weakens the F–F bond.

front_blocks.md: State the colours and physical states of Cl<sub>2</sub>, Br<sub>2</sub> and I<sub>2</sub> at room temperature.

back_blocks.md: **Cl**<sub>**2**</sub> is a yellow-green gas. **Br**<sub>**2**</sub> is an orange-brown liquid. **I**<sub>**2**</sub> is a grey-black solid. The colours of the halogens get darker going down Group 17.

front_blocks.md: Iodine is more volatile than fluorine.

back_blocks.md: **Fluorine** is the most volatile halogen and **iodine** is the least volatile. Iodine has stronger van der Waals' forces between its larger molecules, making it harder to vaporise.

front_blocks.md: Halogens are **..........**  molecules held together between molecules by weak **..........**  forces.

back_blocks.md: Halogens are **diatomic** molecules held together between molecules by weak **instantaneous dipole-induced dipole (van der Waals')** forces.

cards.front_md: Halogens are **..........**  molecules held together between molecules by weak **..........**  forces.

front_blocks.md: Why does fluorine have a lower bond enthalpy than expected for its position in Group 17?

back_blocks.md: **Fluorine** atoms are very small. When two F atoms bond, their **lone pairs** are so close together that they cause significant **repulsion**, counteracting the attraction of the bonding pair to the nuclei. This weakens the F–F bond, giving fluorine an unexpectedly low bond enthalpy.

front_blocks.md: How do instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces explain the trend in volatility across Group 17?

back_blocks.md: Larger halogen molecules have more **electrons**, creating stronger **instantaneous dipole-induced dipole** forces. These require more energy to overcome, raising boiling points and **decreasing volatility** going down the group from F<sub>2</sub> to I<sub>2</sub>.
